# built-in statistics, computed in-process (agents/analysis_agent.standard_stats)
def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked, time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            pairs = [("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None)]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

# built-in statistics, computed in-process (agents/analysis_agent.standard_stats)
def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked, time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            pairs = [("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None)]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

anomaly_alerts.description: Read as HR data (headcount, FTE, separations, attrition rate, voluntary attrition, hires, average salary (current staff)). Headcount is the people in force at the latest date (contractors and agency workers out, interns and part-timers in); separations and hires are events (a rehire's exits count separately); attrition is separations ÷ the average of the month-end headcounts over the 12 months to that date. Pay and protected attributes (gender, ethnicity) are never shown for groups of fewer than 11 people. Gender is shown as a description only: hiring, firing or pay decisions on it are discrimination, so no recommendation is made on it; groups of fewer than 11 people are not shown. Ethnicity is special-category data (GDPR Art. 9): shown as a description only, never a recommendation about people, and never for groups of fewer than 11. Performance ratings describe groups here; they are never used to rank or predict individuals. Pay is annual base salary as recorded: part-time salaries are not full-time equivalents, so groups with more part-timers (often women) show lower pay than on a full-time-equivalent basis, which the unadjusted pay gap uses; pay is never shown for a group of fewer than 11 people.

# built-in statistics, computed in-process (agents/analysis_agent.standard_stats)
def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked, time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,

# built-in statistics, computed in-process (agents/analysis_agent.standard_stats)
def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked, time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            pairs = [("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None)]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

# built-in statistics, computed in-process (agents/analysis_agent.standard_stats)
def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked, time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            pairs = [("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None)]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked, time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:

            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why

                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            pairs = [("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None)]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":

                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:

                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:

                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)

                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]

                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):

                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)

            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap

                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked, time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            pairs = [("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None)]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]

                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:

                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)

                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked, time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend

            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:

            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue

            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            pairs = [("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None)]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]

                                                    for a, b in top]})

            'results': [{'name': str(k), 'value': round(float(v), 2)} for k, v in grp.items()]
        })
    # Headcount by segment
    for seg in seg_cols:
        sub = employees_only[[seg, 'Emp_ID']].dropna()
        grp = sub.groupby(seg)['Emp_ID'].count().nlargest(10)
        result['segments'].append({
            'segment_column': seg,
            'metric_column': 'Emp_ID',
            'aggregation': 'count',
            'label': 'headcount',
            'results': [{'name': str(k), 'value': float(v)} for k, v in grp.items()]
        })
    # Attrition rate by Department using domain facts
    dept_avg_hc = {'Support': 56.2, 'Sales': 95.2, 'Marketing': 37.7, 'Finance': 28.2, 'Engineering': 82.6, 'Operations': 43.1}
    exits = df[df['exit_in_window'] == 'yes'].copy()
    exits_emp = exits[~exits['Worker_Type'].str.lower().isin(
        ['contractor','contingent','agency','agency worker','consultant','freelancer','vendor','contract worker','temp agency']
    )]
    dept_exits = exits_emp.groupby('Department')['Emp_ID'].count()
    attr_results = []
    for dept, avg_hc in dept_avg_hc.items():
        n_exits = dept_exits.get(dept, 0)
        rate = float(n_exits) / avg_hc if avg_hc > 0 else 0.0
        attr_results.append({'name': dept, 'value': round(rate, 4)})
    result['segments'].append({
        'segment_column': 'Department',
        'metric_column': 'exit_in_window',
        'aggregation': 'ratio',
        'label': 'attrition_rate',
        'results': attr_results
    })
    # Attrition rate by year
    exits_all = df[df['exit_event_date'].notna() & (df['exit_event_date'] != '')].copy()
    exits_all['exit_event_date'] = pd.to_datetime(exits_all['exit_event_date'], errors='coerce')
    exits_emp_all = exits_all[~exits_all['Worker_Type'].str.lower().isin(
        ['contractor','contingent','agency','agency worker','consultant','freelancer','vendor','contract worker','temp agency']
    )]
    year_avg_hc = {2024: 343.5, 2025: 337.6, 2026: 344.8}
    exits_emp_all['exit_year'] = exits_emp_all['exit_event_date'].dt.year
    year_exits = exits_emp_all.groupby('exit_year')['Emp_ID'].count()
    yr_results = []
    for yr, avg_hc in year_avg_hc.items():
        n = year_exits.get(yr, 0)
        rate = float(n) / avg_hc if avg_hc > 0 else 0.0
        yr_results.append({'name': str(yr), 'value': round(rate, 4)})
    result['segments'].append({
        'segment_column': 'exit_event_date',
        'metric_column': 'exit_event_date',
        'aggregation': 'ratio',
        'label': 'attrition_rate_by_year',
        'results': yr_results
    })
    # Pay gap by Gender (unadjusted, FTE-equivalent, in_force, >=11 per group)
    pg = employees_only[employees_only['Base_Salary'].notna() & (employees_only['FTE'] > 0)].copy()
    pg['fte_salary'] = pg['Base_Salary'] / pg['FTE']
    gender_grp = pg.groupby('Gender')['fte_salary']
    gender_counts = gender_grp.count()
    valid_genders = gender_counts[gender_counts >= 11].index
    pg_valid = pg[pg['Gender'].isin(valid_genders)]
    mean_by_gender = pg_valid.groupby('Gender')['fte_salary'].mean()
    median_by_gender = pg_valid.groupby('Gender')['fte_salary'].median()
    result['segments'].append({
        'segment_column': 'Gender',
        'metric_column': 'Base_Salary',
        'aggregation': 'mean',
        'label': 'mean_fte_salary_unadjusted',
        'results': [{'name': str(k), 'value': round(float(v), 2)} for k, v in mean_by_gender.items()]
    })
    result['segments'].append({
        'segment_column': 'Gender',
        'metric_column': 'Base_Salary',
        'aggregation': 'mean',
        'label': 'median_fte_salary_unadjusted',
        'results': [{'name': str(k), 'value': round(float(v), 2)} for k, v in median_by_gender.items()]
    })
except Exception:
    pass

# ANOMALIES
try:
    anomaly_count = 0
    for col in ['FTE', 'Base_Salary']:
        vals = df[col].dropna()
        if vals.nunique() < 5:
            continue
        skew = float(vals.skew())
        if abs(skew) > 2:
            shift = max(0, -vals.min())
            transformed = np.log1p(vals + shift)
        else:
            transformed = vals.copy()
            shift = 0
        q1, q3 = transformed.quantile(0.25), transformed.quantile(0.75)
        iqr = q3 - q1
        lo, hi = q1 - 3 * iqr, q3 + 3 * iqr
        flagged = transformed[(transformed < lo) | (transformed > hi)]
        frac = len(flagged) / len(vals)
        if frac > 0.05:
            result['anomalies'].append({
                'column': col, 'row_index': None, 'value': None,
                'expected_range': f'{float(vals.quantile(0.25)):.2f}–{float(vals.quantile(0.75)):.2f}',
                'severity': 'low',
                'explanation': f'{col} is heavy-tailed; extreme-value flagging skipped'
            })
            continue
        orig_lo = float(np.expm1(lo) - shift) if abs(skew) > 2 else float(lo)
        orig_hi = float(np.expm1(hi) - shift) if abs(skew) > 2 else float(hi)
        for idx in flagged.index:
            if anomaly_count >= 25:
                break
            orig_val = float(df.loc[idx, col])
            t_val = float(transformed[idx])
            lo4 = q1 - 4 * iqr; hi4 = q3 + 4 * iqr
            lo5 = q1 - 5 * iqr; hi5 = q3 + 5 * iqr
            if t_val > hi5 or t_val < lo5:
                sev = 'critical'
            elif t_val > hi4 or t_val < lo4:
                sev = 'high'
            else:
                sev = 'medium'
            result['anomalies'].append({
                'column': col, 'row_index': int(idx), 'value': orig_val,
                'expected_range': f'{orig_lo:.2f}–{orig_hi:.2f}',
                'severity': sev,
                'explanation': f'{col} value {orig_val} lies outside expected range {orig_lo:.2f}–{orig_hi:.2f}'
            })
            anomaly_count += 1
except Exception:
    pass

# TRENDS (MoM on monthly snapshots, per-month last value per employee then sum)
try:
    df['snap_month'] = df['Snapshot_Date'].dt.to_period('M')
    monthly_last = df.sort_values('Snapshot_Date').groupby(['Emp_ID', 'snap_month']).last().reset_index()
    emp_only_monthly = monthly_last[~monthly_last['Worker_Type'].str.lower().isin(
        ['contractor','contingent','agency','agency worker','consultant','freelancer','vendor','contract worker','temp agency']
    )]
    for col in ['FTE', 'Base_Salary']:
        monthly_sum = emp_only_monthly.groupby('snap_month')[col].sum().sort_index()
        if len(monthly_sum) >= 2:
            pct = float((monthly_sum.iloc[-1] - monthly_sum.iloc[-2]) / monthly_sum.iloc[-2] * 100) if monthly_sum.iloc[-2] != 0 else 0.0
            direction = 'up' if pct > 0.5 else ('down' if pct < -0.5 else 'flat')
            result['trends'].append({
                'column': col, 'period': 'MoM', 'direction': direction,
                'pct_change': round(pct, 4), 'segment': None
            })
except Exception:
    pass

# FORECASTING (simple linear extrapolation of monthly Base_Salary sum, next 3 months)
try:
    monthly_sal = emp_only_monthly.groupby('snap_month')['Base_Salary'].sum().sort_index()
    if len(monthly_sal) >= 6:
        x = np.arange(len(monthly_sal))
        y = monthly_sal.values.astype(float)
        slope, intercept, _, _, _ = stats.linregress(x, y)
        last_period = monthly_sal.index[-1]
        for i in range(1, 4):
            future_period = last_period + i
            pred = float(intercept + slope * (len(monthly_sal) - 1 + i))
            result['forecast_points'].append({
                'period': str(future_period),
                'value': round(pred, 2)
            })
except Exception:
    pass

result['assumptions'] = [
    'Correlations and current-staff metrics use one row per Emp_ID (latest snapshot) to avoid double-counting.',
    'Attrition rates use domain-fact average headcounts; exits counted via exit_in_window and exit_event_date flags.',
    'Pay gap is unadjusted FTE-equivalent salary (Base_Salary / FTE); groups with <11 people excluded.',
    'Contractors/agency workers excluded from headcount, FTE sums, salary and attrition per domain rules.',
    'Trend and forecast use monthly last-snapshot-per-employee sums; heavy-tailed columns noted, not flagged.'
]

anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as HR data (headcount, FTE, separations, attrition rate, hires, average salary (current staff)). Headcount is the people in force at the latest date (contractors and agency workers out, interns and part-timers in); separations and hires are events (a rehire's exits count separately); attrition is separations ÷ the average of the month-end headcounts over the 12 months to that date. Pay and protected attributes (gender, ethnicity) are never shown for groups of fewer than 11 people. Gender is shown as a description only: hiring, firing or pay decisions on it are discrimination, so no recommendation is made on it; groups of fewer than 11 people are not shown. Pay is annual base salary as recorded: part-time salaries are not full-time equivalents, so groups with more part-timers (often women) show lower pay than on a full-time-equivalent basis, which the unadjusted pay gap uses; pay is never shown for a group of fewer than 11 people.

executive_view.headline: A 353-person workforce is growing and retaining staff better: attrition fell to 14.3% in the 12 months to Oct 2026, down from 20.9% the prior year, while overall Full Time Equivalent rose year-on-year.

paragraphs.text: Sales stands out as the one department where both Full Time Equivalent and Base Salary declined year-on-year, while attrition there remains the highest of any department.

findings.text: Attrition improved sharply: the 12-month rate to Oct 2026 is 14.3%, down from 20.9% the prior year, with 70 hires against 49 separations in the most recent 12-month window.

Sales is the only department contracting: Full Time Equivalent fell year-on-year and month-on-month, Base Salary also fell year-on-year, and its attrition rate of 22.1% is the highest across all departments.
Operations and Marketing are the fastest-growing departments by Full Time Equivalent year-on-year, and both also saw strong Base Salary growth over the same period.

The workforce is split across Remote (110), Austin (82), New York (82) and London (79) locations, with 313 full employees and 40 part-timers; unadjusted Base Salary figures for part-timer-heavy groups will appear lower than a full-time-equivalent comparison would show.
